en: Mia is a girl, so we use “She”.
Tom has a sled. ___ rides it down the hill.
Tom is a boy, so we use “He”.
The snail is slow. ___ moves bit by bit.
There is one snail, so we use “It”.
Sam and Lily are friends. ___ walk to school together.
Sam and Lily are two people, so we use “They”.
My sister and I made a cake. ___ ate it all.
“My sister and I” includes me, so we use “We”.
It is Tom’s birthday. I gave ___ a present.
Tom is a boy, and the word comes after “gave”, so we use “him”.
Grandma likes flowers, so we picked some for ___.
Grandma is a woman, so we use “her”.
The puppies are hungry. Let’s feed ___.
There are many puppies, so we use “them”.
Look at the moon! ___ is so bright tonight.
The moon is one thing, so we use “It”.
Which word can we use instead of “the boys”?
“The boys” means more than one person, so we use “they”.
Dad is cooking. ___ is making soup.
Dad is a man, so we use “He”.
The kite is up high. ___ is flying in the wind.
The kite is one thing, so we use “It”.
Ella and I are sisters. ___ share a room.
“Ella and I” includes me, so we use “We”.
I can see the swans. Can you see ___?
There are many swans, so we use “them”.
Mum is tired. Let’s make ___ a cup of tea.
Mum is a woman, so we use “her”.
Grandpa told a funny story. We all laughed with ___.
Grandpa is a man, so we use “him”.
The flowers are pretty. ___ are red and yellow.
There are many flowers, so we use “They”.
Which word can we use instead of “Lucy”?
Lucy is one girl, so we use “she”.
Which word can we use instead of “the umbrella”?
The umbrella is one thing, so we use “it”.
My friends and I went to the park. ___ had a picnic.
“My friends and I” includes me, so we use “We”.
The elephant is big. ___ has long tusks.
There is one elephant, so we use “It”.
Leo lost his hat. Can you help ___ find it?
Leo is a boy, so we use “him”.
The bees are busy. ___ make honey.
There are many bees, so we use “They”.
Aunt Rosa sent me a card. I wrote back to ___.
Aunt Rosa is a woman, so we use “her”.
I have two goldfish. I feed ___ every day.
There are two goldfish, so we use “them”.
Which word can we use instead of “Mr Lee”?
Mr Lee is a man, so we use “he”.
You and I are a team! ___ will win together.
“You and I” includes me, so we use “We”.
The penguin slid on the ice. ___ landed on its tummy.
There is one penguin, so we use “It”.
Zoe and Max are twins. ___ have the same birthday.
Zoe and Max are two people, so we use “They”.
Which word can we use instead of “my brother and I”?
“My brother and I” includes me, so we use “we”.

example.why_en: Mia is a girl, so we use “She”.

en.title: He, she, it and they
en.teach: We can use a short word instead of a name: he, she, it, they and we. Mia is happy. She is playing. Him, her and them come after the action: I saw Tom. I saw him.
